sentences.text: Its volatility was 72.2% a year, measured on monthly returns in pounds from the end of Dec 2014 to the end of Sep 2026.
Over the same months, the tracker's was 11.7%.
Volatility measures how widely returns swung around their average, up as well as down. It describes the past, not the future.
Since the end of Dec 2014, its largest fall, measured at month-end, was 74.2%: from its high at the end of Dec 2017 to its low at the end of Jan 2019, 13 months later.
£10,000 invested at that high would have been worth £2,580 at the low, £7,420 less.
It was back at that high by the end of Oct 2020, 21 months after the low and 34 months after the high.
Falls are measured from one month-end to the next, so a fall that recovered within a month doesn't show. The £10,000 figure applies only to money invested at the high.
Global financial crisis (end of Sep 2007 to end of Mar 2009): not covered; its history in pounds starts at the end of Dec 2014.
The tracker: not covered.
Covid crash (end of Jan 2020 to end of Mar 2020): down 27.0% over the period.
The tracker: down 14.5% over the same period.
2022 rate shock (end of Dec 2021 to end of Oct 2022): down 47.7% over the period.
The tracker: down 6.0% over the same period.
Each figure compares the start and end of the period. Prices may have fallen further in between and partly recovered.

Its correlation with the tracker was 0.39, measured on monthly returns in pounds from the end of Dec 2014 to the end of Sep 2026: 1 would mean always moving in step, 0 no pattern, and −1 always opposite.
Measured over each 36-month stretch, it ranged from 0.24 (the 36 months to the end of Dec 2021) to 0.60 (the 36 months to the end of Feb 2025).
Correlation says how consistently the monthly moves lined up, not how big they were. A low figure is not protection.

As an illustration, not a recommendation: from the end of Dec 2014 to the end of Sep 2026, a mix of 90% in the tracker and 10% in this investment, reset to 90/10 at the end of every December, returned 24.8% a year, against 12.8% a year for the tracker alone.
The mix's volatility was 18.4% against the tracker's 11.7%, and its largest fall at month-end was 19.9% against 15.0%.
Before fees, trading costs and tax.

sentences.text: From the end of Dec 2014 to the end of Sep 2026: up 26,595.8% in dollars, and the dollar rose 17.4% against the pound, so in pounds it was up 31,244.5%.
Covid crash: down 31.4% in dollars, the dollar rose 6.5%, so down 27.0% in pounds.
2022 rate shock: down 55.7% in dollars, the dollar rose 17.9%, so down 47.7% in pounds.
The two parts multiply rather than add, so they never simply add up to the figure in pounds.

sentences.text: It is not issued or backed by a government or a company, and it pays no income. Its price can move a long way in days, it trades around the clock, and holdings can be lost to theft or lost keys. Its history here starts at the end of Dec 2014, so it covers fewer market conditions than the others.
These are past results in pounds, measured at month-ends, before platform fees, trading costs and tax. Past behaviour does not predict future results.
